role_agent_name: First Nations and regional community liaison (LIAIS)
abstract: Maintains records on traditional territorial access protocols and community consultation feedback
system_message:
You are First Nations and regional community liaison (LIAIS). The First Nations and regional community liaison (LIAIS) maintains records on traditional territorial access protocols and community consultation feedback, and tracks compliance with archaeological heritage surveillance standards across slope stabilization options in the Fraser Canyon corridor.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Archaeological heritage surveillance（HERIT）
information_points.content:
LIAIS-HERIT-IE6：For the High-tensile drapery mesh with hollow-core rock bolts scheme, the heritage buffer setback distance provides a minimum linear separation of 75 m from recorded cultural heritage features along the historic river terrace perimeter.
LIAIS-HERIT-O5Y：For the Prestressed ground anchors with sculpted shotcrete scheme, the heritage buffer setback distance maintains a minimum linear separation of 100 m from recorded cultural heritage features along the historic river terrace perimeter.
LIAIS-HERIT-NH5：For the Dynamic rockfall barrier fence with horizontal drain arrays scheme, the heritage buffer setback distance provides a minimum linear separation of 50 m from recorded cultural heritage features along the historic river terrace perimeter.

information_points.title: Maintains records on traditional territorial access protocols and community consultation feedback（COMM）
information_points.content:
LIAIS-COMM-08X：For the Dynamic rockfall barrier fence with horizontal drain arrays scheme, the Indigenous heritage monitor participation rating reaches 96% of active work shifts attended by accredited community cultural monitors under Fraser Canyon First Nations observer deployment.
LIAIS-COMM-I4D：For the High-tensile drapery mesh with hollow-core rock bolts scheme, the Indigenous heritage monitor participation rating is 85% of active work shifts attended by accredited community cultural monitors during Fraser Canyon First Nations observer deployment.
LIAIS-COMM-EKY：For the Prestressed ground anchors with sculpted shotcrete scheme, the Indigenous heritage monitor participation rating stands at 85% of active work shifts attended by accredited community cultural monitors under the Fraser Canyon First Nations observer deployment.
